messages:
maria: Heads-up — thinking about a pattern for per-tenant telemetry isolation. TL;DR: tenant namespace routing at OTLP ingress, route to tenant-specific storage (indices/buckets), enforce retention per-tenant, and RBAC on query. Want feedback on feasibility + major gotchas.

sam: +1 to namespace routing. main choices are: route in the collector vs centralize then fan-out in a worker. collector routing is simpler for isolation but increases collector config churn.

nisha: question: where do we enforce quotas? at OTLP ingestion (reject/throttle) or later (ingest everything, charge later)? leaning ingestion-side throttling for cost control.

lee: privacy: we need scrubbers before fan-out. some tenants send PII in attributes. We should run an attributes processor to drop/mask keys based on tenant policy.

sam: rough otel-collector processor/exporter idea:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
processors:
  attributes/tenant_routing:
    actions:
      - key: tenant.id
        from: resource
  filter_by_tenant:
    match_type: strict
exporters:
  tenant_a_s3:
    type: s3
    bucket: telemetry-tenant-a
  shared_bigstore:
    type: s3
    bucket: telemetry-shared
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes/tenant_routing, filter_by_tenant]
      exporters: [tenant_a_s3, shared_bigstore]
```
sam: route selection would be a simple conditional on resource.attributes.tenant.id; if missing -> send to shared bucket + emit alert.

maria: fallback seems important. We should surface missing tenant mappings in console (red flag) and auto-create a placeholder dataset with very short retention until human review.

nisha: retention enforcement: prefer storage-layer lifecycle policies (ES ILM, S3 lifecycle) rather than deleting in-flight. Simpler and auditable. For ES: index per tenant -> apply ILM policy. For object stores: prefix per-tenant, bucket lifecycle rules.

lee: RBAC: two layers: storage IAM (per-tenant service account) + query-layer enforcement (console/API checks tenant scope). We can't rely on index prefixes alone for query-time auth.

sam: edge case: high-cardinality tenants (millions of small tenants). Creating buckets/indices per tenant doesn't scale. Options:
- shard by namespace group (tenant shards) + tenant_id in index docs + strict query filtering at query layer
- use multi-tenant shared store but enforce isolation via per-tenant encryption keys and access policies
We should pick hybrid: dedicated datasets for top 500 paying tenants, shared sharded backing for long tail.

maria: agree hybrid. also: telemetry cost accounting — we need per-tenant token counters at ingestion to support billing + quota. Can export metrics to billing pipeline.

nisha: technical note: use the otelcollector "metrics" + prometheus exporter to emit tenant ingestion counters. Beware cardinality explosion; emit aggregated counters by billing-tiers.

infra-bot: created task INFRA-382: "tenant-telemetry-routing PoC" and INFRA-383: "retention + lifecycle per-tenant" assigned to @sam and @nisha. :white_check_mark:

sam: for rollout: PoC with 2 tenants -> dedicated indices + one shared fallback. Validate RBAC and retention. Canary ingestion for 24h, then run cost sim for 7d.

lee: security reqs: document data-handling for each tenant (PII patterns), run SAST on the collector config templates, and include an opt-in scrub policy per tenant.

maria: nice. next steps: sam + nisha to drop a minimal PoC collector config + infra terraform sketch by EOD Friday. I'll wire up console flags to show missing dataset alerts. @lee please add privacy checklist items to the task.

sam: will do. attaching quick filter snippet we can reuse: 
```yaml
processors:
  resource/include:
    attributes: ["tenant.id"]
  routing:
    table:
      - from: resource.attributes.tenant.id
        to: "tenant_${value}"
```

maria: thanks all. keeping this thread for progress updates. :rocket:
